messages:
maria.choi: Quick Q — for Private deployments: when service A (proj:alpha) calls service B (proj:beta), what should our recommended auth pattern be? Current long-lived API keys are project-scoped which makes cross-project calls messy. Proposal: short-lived delegated tokens minted by an auth-broker with minimal 'acts_as' claims. Thoughts? @kevin @lina

kevin: SG. Are you thinking mint-on-demand (per-call) or mint once and cache? downside of mint-on-demand is extra hop/higher latency.

maria.choi: Mint-on-demand but via a sidecar/local cache so not every request hits broker. Flow: long-lived service key used to bootstrap -> sidecar gets ephemeral token for target project with expiry ~5m -> sidecar reuses until expiry. Fallback: allow long-lived key only for bootstrap/health checks.

oliver: Perf + complexity caution. If sidecar misses cache we can still blow up latency. Suggest: 1) warm tokens on connection start, 2) reuse per-connection, 3) keep an intermediate cache TTL (e.g., 1h) with revocation list support. That avoids per-request minting.

lina: From billing/audit side we need identity invariants: token must include origin_project, origin_service_id, and acting_claim so attribution and billing match usage. Also need an option to forward audit logs to central stack for Private customers who opt in.

samir: Ops notes — revocation is hard in air-gapped/private setups. We need both TTL-based safety and an invalidation mechanism: push invalidation when outbound allowed, otherwise rely on short TTL + rotation. Also gateway-level guardrails so we can revoke at the ingress if needed.

maria.choi: Agreed. Sketch of token payload (example):

```json
{
  "iss": "auth-broker",
  "sub": "svc-alpha:payment-processor",
  "acts_as": "svc-alpha:payment-client",
  "origin_project": "alpha",
  "target_project": "beta",
  "roles": ["svc-writer"],
  "aud": "service-beta",
  "exp": 1719004800,
  "revocation_id": "rrf-12345"
}
```

maria.choi: Key rules here: small surface for roles (keep role cardinality low), include both origin and target project in token, and include a revocation identifier to allow targeted invalidation.

kevin: For RBAC mapping: map `acts_as` -> runtime roles at gateway. Keep roles coarse to avoid explosion (suggestion: svc-reader, svc-writer, svc-admin, svc-system). More granular permissions should be handled inside the service with service-level checks.

lina: Edge case: third-party/partner projects — allow a `guest` role but require explicit allowlist in the customer's org settings. Also ensure consent capture for audit/billing.

oliver: Policy-eval perf: gateway should do a cheap check (token validity + role in allowed list) using cached policy entries (TTL ~30s). Full ABAC evaluation only when minting new tokens or when policy cache misses. That balances speed and correctness.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: auth-broker v2 canary rolling to cluster `prod-private-1` starting 2024-10-12T14:00Z — health checks enabled.

maria.choi: Next step: I'll draft an RFC follow-up documenting flow diagrams, token schemas, gateway checks, and perf targets. Who volunteers to co-author? @kevin @oliver @lina @samir

kevin: :thumbsup: I'll add perf microbenchmarks and cache-hit targets.

lina: I'll add billing attribution and audit shipping requirements.

samir: I'll cover revocation behavior, sidecar failure modes, and fallback gating.

oliver: Happy to write the gateway policy caching section + example configs.

maria.choi: Awesome. I'll put a draft up by EOD tomorrow and link here. Thanks all :heart:
